notes.title: Shakes on a Plane Now Available on PlayStation and Xbox Consoles
notes.content:
Attention passengers! 
Please return your seats to the upright position, fasten your seat belts and prepare for some crazy antics! 

Together with developer Huu Games we are thrilled to announce that our chaotic couch co-op title Shakes on a Plane is available today for PlayStation 4/5 and Xbox One/Xbox Series X|S. 
The console versions will be available from the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store ([b]with a limited time 20% launch discount for the Xbox version[/b]). 

[b]Shake on a Plane is also available for PC here on Steam and Nintendo Switch. [/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/964620/Shakes_on_a_Plane/

[h3]Watch the console release trailer of Shakes On A Plane on YouTube now:[/h3]
[previewyoutube=I7teReqBF7U;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]About Shakes On A Plane:[/h3]
Have you always dreamed of a life in the clouds, jet-setting from exotic locale to exotic locale, and enjoying the finest international cuisine? Well, how about just the jet-setting part, and instead of enjoying fine cuisine you’re instead serving burgers and shakes to a group of impatient, hangry passengers all crammed together in a metal box thousands of feet in the air? 
Shakes on a Plane tasks you and up to three friends with providing a satisfying airborne culinary experience in a chaotic environment with simple, easy-to-use controls and deceptively tactical gameplay. Coordination, delegation, and teamwork will propel-ler you to victory and ensure a five-star rating on the “How Was Your Flight Today” survey. And if the passengers get too sassy you can always para-drop them out the airlock — trust us, it’s standard procedure for all airlines.

[h3]Shakes on a Plane features Include:[/h3]
[list][*] [u][b]Flying is Fun...Right?:[/b][/u] 
Crying babies, obnoxious drunks, impatient business class fliers...It’s not your job to pick the passengers, but it is your job to keep them satisfied with delicious treats and tasty beverages.
[*] [u][b]Teamwork Makes the Dream Work:[/b][/u] 
Grab up to three other players to build your ideal team of talented flight attendants, but don’t forget that you’re locked with them inside a narrow metal tube at 30,000 feet — coordination, cooperation, and patience are the keys to a successful flight.
[*] [u][b]I Didn’t Order the Fish:[/b][/u] 
Attention to detail is vital to keeping your impatient passengers sated with enough fast food to hopefully put them to sleep for the remainder of the flight. Make sure you get the right order to the right person, on time, or the cabin might get a tad unpleasant…
[*] [u][b]Putting the F in First Class...And UFO:[/b][/u] 
Don’t get too comfortable...each plane has a different layout, forcing players to adapt on the “fly” and perfectly plan their food delivery path.[/list]

notes.title: Couch Co-Op "Shakes on a Plane" will be released on December 15 on Steam
notes.content:
📢 Dear passengers, an important announcement: 
Together with developer Huu Games we announce that the couch co-op title [i][b]Shakes on a Plane[/b][/i] will be postponed on December 15 for PC on Steam.

💡 Due to technical difficulties, the Takeoff and release of Shakes on a Plane needed to be moved!
In order to provide you with the best possible and most fun co-op gaming experience, the new release date for Shakes on a Plane will be December 15 on Steam for PC together with the release for Nintendo Switch.
Until then, play the Steam demo or sit back and watch the publisher stream, featured in our Steam broadcast.

[h3]Wishlist the game, play the free demo and watch our 4-player coop broadcast on Steam[/h3]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/964620/Shakes_on_a_Plane/


[h3]What is Shakes on a Plane?[/h3]
[i][b]Shakes on a Plane[/b][/i] is a chaotic, cooperative multiplayer game in the style of Overcooked for one to four players via split-screen or "Steam Remote Play Together" feature. 
[i][b]In Shakes on a Plane[/b][/i], players take on the role of the cabin crew on various aircraft and serve a variety of delicious shakes, burgers, French fries and many other dishes under time pressure before the plane lands and passengers evaluate the players' performance. 
In [b]27 levels[/b] the players travel around the world several times. 
Literally, because [i][b]Shakes on a Plane[/b][/i] is playable in [b]all 29 available languages on Steam[/b]. The levels are designed to be varied and always offer new challenges. 
Those who think that this game only serves dishes are mistaken. Throw passengers and their luggage out of the plane, watch out for turbulence and serving trolleys, or use the individual skills of the game characters. For example, shooing passengers out of the way, fast jumps forward, throwing objects or turning yourself into a box to protect yourself from moving serving trolleys. Shakes on a Plane offers a colourful mix of levels and features for unimagined gaming fun and boundless hatred to other players!

[h3]Features:[/h3]
[list][*] Serve your passengers with up to four players and cooperate in convincing them that flying with you is always a good decision.
[*] The orders vary from shakes, burgers, coffee and even a greater variety of fast food which underlines only the best quality you offer for your passengers.
[*] Time is essential and your guests have a high demand of multiple goods all the flight long. Grab tablets to solve various orders at the same time and don’t let them wait too long.
[*] Not only turmoils might occur during your flights, walking passengers, moving tables and many more things will complicate your accomplishments on your planes.[/list]

notes.title: Short December progress update!
notes.content:
Shakes on a plane is making good progress: we have just about finished all the raw level content, and are now adding "secondary mechanics" such as alien passengers and ragdolls to the game.  Currently with the alien passengers bugging out the cabin looks like a scene from The Thing (hmmh... there's an idea...)

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33907858/cef718997f2ae03852e1b2fbdf150f98bae9f0a6.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33907858/6656a4fea11c53ac8e451a2b3b58febeff36a712.png[/img][/url]

Scary, isn't it?

Of course the level content needs much more testing and balancing, and we are hoping to start closed alpha testing soon. The challenge is to design and balance the levels so that they will support varied amount of players. For this, we have a mechanism in place that adjust the difficulty per player count: this includes tweaking things like order frequency, turbulence alarm time etc. What we don't want to do is to alter the level itself per player count, and so far it seems we don't have to.

Other huge area we are making progress in are the cinematics. I'd say we have more to show on that front soon.
